description: Search FDA drug application records: Drugs@FDA approvals (NDAs, ANDAs, BLAs) with sponsor and full submission history by default, or with dataset the Orange Book's patents and exclusivities, or FDA's Complete Response Letters with their full text. Pair with openfda_get_drug_label to read the approved label, or openfda_count_values to aggregate by sponsor_name, product_type, or route. With stage=true, call openfda_dataframe_describe for the staged columns, then openfda_dataframe_query for SQL.

canvas_id.description: canvas_id from an earlier staged call to openfda_search_* or openfda_lookup_ndc: stages this call onto that canvas too (as stage=true does), so its tables can be joined.

cursor.description: next_cursor from the previous page, with no skip and the same search, sort, and endpoint as that call; other inputs may change.

dataset.description: drugsfda: Drugs@FDA applications, each with its sponsor, products, and submission history. orangebook: Orange Book product records, one per strength, with patents[], exclusivity[], and therapeutic equivalence codes. crl: Complete Response Letters FDA issued on drug and biologic applications, each with its full text.

fields.description: Dotted record paths to keep on each record, e.g. ["sponsor_name", "submissions.submission_status_date"], plus its identity key (application_number, products.application_number, products.application_type, product_number, file_name, letter_date). Any record path works (openfda_describe_fields lists searchable ones); a path through an array covers every element. Use it when page_bytes flags an oversized record; with stage=true only the inline page is projected.

limit.description: Records per page. A Drugs@FDA record carries its application's whole submission history, so a long-running application is an order of magnitude larger than a recent one, and a letter carries its full text. Default and cap by dataset: drugsfda 25 (cap 375), orangebook 25 (cap 1000), crl 5 (cap 75); a larger value returns at most that cap and says so.

search.description: openFDA search query, e.g. products.brand_name:"eliquis" (any letter case; openfda.* fields are filled only on harmonized applications, so openfda.brand_name misses the rest), sponsor_name:"PFIZER" (stored uppercase; a lowercase quoted value returns no matches); on orangebook products.brand_name:"ELIQUIS", patents.expiration_date:[20270101 TO 20271231]; on crl application_number:"NDA 210274", text:"bioequivalence". openFDA tests each clause against the whole record, so AND-ed clauses on one array's fields can be met by different entries (an ORIG submission and a PRIORITY one); to require one entry, stage the search and filter per entry in openfda_dataframe_query. Each dataset spells an application number its own way: a letter's "NDA 210274" is Drugs@FDA's NDA210274 and the Orange Book's products.application_number:"210274" with products.application_type:"N" ("A" for an ANDA); a letter matches only its whole stored spelling (no wildcard reaches the number past the space). Omit to browse newest first. A "+" between clauses reads as a space; inside a quoted phrase it is a literal plus.

skip.description: Records to skip, at most 25000; to read past that, follow next_cursor from skip 0.

sort.description: A field path with :asc or :desc (any letter case; :ascending and :descending also work), several comma-separated. With neither search nor sort, records come newest first by submissions.submission_status_date:desc (an application's latest submission status date, supplements included, not its approval date; approval_date:desc on orangebook, letter_date:desc on crl). A search without sort returns openFDA's index order, not relevance.

stage.description: Also stage the matched set on a DataCanvas for SQL: openfda_dataframe_describe lists its columns, then openfda_dataframe_query runs the SQL. Staging is bounded (staged_rows says how many rows landed); for a distribution over the whole match, use openfda_count_values.

name: openfda_search_drug_approvals

canvas_id.description: Canvas id of the staged set: pass to openfda_dataframe_describe, openfda_dataframe_query, or a later staged search.

canvas_table.description: Staged table name: openfda_dataframe_describe lists its columns, then use it in openfda_dataframe_query.

effectiveQuery.description: Search filter applied to the selected dataset, as submitted to openFDA

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `limit_above_cap`: limit exceeds the cap of the endpoint this call selects, on a deployment that rejects rather than clamps it. `canvas_disabled`: Staging was requested (stage=true or a canvas_id) but DataCanvas is disabled. `canvas_not_found`: The canvas_id is well-formed but names no active canvas — expired or never minted. `canvas_capacity_exhausted`: canvas_id was omitted and the active canvas cap is already reached. `rate_limited`: The openFDA daily or per-minute request limit is exceeded. `upstream_error`: The openFDA API returned a 5xx error, or a 200 that is not openFDA JSON. `malformed_search`: search leaves a double quote, parenthesis, or range bracket unclosed, ends on a backslash, or holds a character openFDA refuses. `query_error`: The search query was rejected by openFDA (malformed field name, invalid syntax). `pagination_limit_reached`: skip exceeds the 25000 record pagination ceiling. `invalid_cursor`: cursor does not decode, belongs to another endpoint, search, or sort, or comes with skip above 0, stage, or canvas_id. `not_sortable`: openFDA refused a key in sort: analyzed text, an .exact form the field lacks, a field with no sortable form, or one the endpoint lacks. Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

recovery.description: Actionable next step for the caller.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

limit.description: Page size applied: limit, the endpoint default, or the cap when limit exceeded it. The last page of a match holds fewer records.

totalUnverified.description: True on an empty page at skip > 0 whose total could not be confirmed: total 0 then does not rule out records — re-call with skip=0.

next_cursor.description: Pass as cursor for the next page; present on a page read at skip 0 or by cursor when more records follow and openFDA can continue the walk.

notice.description: Guidance for this page: empty result, limit clamp, end of a cursor walk, fields projection, oversized record, staging, SQL for AND-ed clauses on one array entry. Absent when nothing needs saying.

page_bytes.description: UTF-8 size of results; present only when a record exceeds 24000 bytes, with page_largest_fields.

page_largest_fields.description: The largest record's biggest fields, largest first, beside page_bytes. Leave them out with fields.

bytes.description: UTF-8 bytes, summed across array elements.

path.description: Dotted path; array elements share one path (patient.drug.openfda covers every drug).

projected_fields.description: Paths each record was projected to, present only with fields; a field missing from a record was projected away, not absent upstream.

results.description: Records of the selected dataset. Drug application records — application_number, sponsor_name, openfda block on harmonized applications only (brand_name, generic_name, route, product_type, substance_name), products[] (brand_name, active_ingredients, dosage_form, marketing_status), submissions[] (submission_type, submission_status, submission_status_date, review_priority). Orange Book products — product_number, approval_date (approved_prior_to_1982 on older products), products[] (application_type, application_number, brand_name, active_ingredients, therapeutic_equivalence_codes, reference_listed_drug), patents[] (patent_number, expiration_date, patent_use_code), exclusivity[] (exclusivity_code, exclusivity_expiration_date). Letters — application_number[], letter_date (MM/DD/YYYY), letter_type, approval_status, company_name, company_address, approver_name, file_name, text.

spilled.description: True when this call staged its matched set; see canvas_id.

staged_rows.description: Rows written to the canvas table; below meta.total, the table holds only the first staged_rows records.

totalResults.description: Total matching records in the selected dataset

truncated.description: True when staging stopped short of meta.total; narrow the search for the whole set.

truncated_by.description: Why staging stopped short of meta.total (upstream_end: openFDA served no more records). Only when truncated is.

title: Openfda Search Drug Approvals
